newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs saved by the bell, PS key to Monday mood.
newsitem.headline: OLOs saved by the bell, PS key to Monday mood.

text.p: Belgian linear bond futures trading, which on Friday closed just in time to miss a 40-bp sell off in Bund futures, is seen catching up with Germany on Monday, dealers said.

The front-month OLO future ended two bp higher at 123.13 at 1600 GMT. By 1630 GMT, Bund futures stood 37 bp lower at 103.27, after touching 103.15, in what dealers descirbed as a technical sell off in low volume.
Monday's mood will also be determined by the outcome of this weekend's leadership congress of the francophone socialist PS party, one of the four parties in the centre-left coalition.
PS chairman Philippe Busquin will seek re-election, but is expected to get a limited term of only a few months.
"I hope that he will not be pushed aside by one of the more extreme regionalist leaders in the PS," one OLO dealer said.

The Belgian franc, which weakened to 20.64 to the mark midweek, ended at 20.6310/25, after firming to 20.6255/75 in the morning. Dealers said that the market remained nervous about the political situation, which is why short-term yields remain well above the central bank's 3.00 percent central rate. One-week repos ended at 3.40/50 percent, three-month bills at 3.35/45 percent.
